$comment: Component tokens reference semantic tokens only — never primitives, never raw values.

button.$comment: Mono uppercase always carries the wide label tracking — without it the caps set too tight to read.
button.$comment-pressed: Pressed is the inverse of hover — the sticker settles back down. It resolves to the resting values in every theme, so a theme that lifts collapses the lift, and one that brightens (Adventure) drops back to no bump.
button.$comment-spinner: Loading spinner — a ring in the button's own text color (currentColor) that spins while an action is in flight. Sized to the inline icon so it sits where a leading icon would; ambient duration/easing because it is a continuous, non-reactive loop, the same motion category as the danger drift.

primary.$comment: Ink border is a global sticker rule — primary and secondary differ by fill, not by outline. The hard shadow extrudes from this edge.

button.$comment-danger: Danger is primary's shape in a different register: same footprint, same ink border, but the fill is the DANGER status rather than the brand — so it is caution tape in every theme, whatever the brand is doing. The hazard stripes are a background-image over that fill, in black on the yellow ground; the stripe geometry is a token so the texture scales with the system rather than being a magic number in the CSS.

stripe-width.comment: 8px band, so the diagonal repeats every 16px

stripe-duration.comment: one full pass of the pattern

danger.$comment-label-plate: Full-contrast stripes and a black label cannot share one ground — the diagonals cut straight through the text. So the label sits on a solid plate of the fill, which is what printed hazard tape does too: the stripes frame the thing, the words stay on clean colour.

label-pad-x.comment: 8px — one stripe-width of clear colour either side of the label

label-pad-y.comment: 4px — enough that a diagonal never clips an ascender or a descender
